title: Redact retained duplicate-triage records on account deletion
owner_decision: Delete user data, retain security/audit logs; retain household chat messages with anonymized authors.
classification: Confirmed privacy leak fixed: retained DuplicateFixLog rows cleared the actor foreign key but kept actor-owned filesystem paths and account identifiers in free-text notes.

change.selection: Rows are selected when the deleted account is the actor or its name, email, or user ID appears case-insensitively in the folder path or notes; SQL LIKE metacharacters in identifiers are escaped.
change.retention: Duplicate action and match metadata remain. Actor references are cleared, account identifiers in notes are replaced with [deleted account], and absolute paths in matching notes or folder_path values are replaced with [redacted path].

verification.pre_fix_reproduction: On a fresh database at Alembic head, the new deletion regression failed because the actor-owned Windows folder path remained in DuplicateFixLog.folder_path.
verification.result: passed: 6 tests on Python 3.14.10 and PostgreSQL 17.6
verification.coverage: Actor-owned mixed-case email and Windows/POSIX paths are redacted; unlinked rows matching a case-variant email are selected, their path is redacted, and their note is anonymized. Existing deletion and FK inventory regressions pass.
verification.database: Fresh oneirodexdupfixpost_test database upgraded from Alembic baseline through head; dropped after verification. TEST_DATABASE_URL was process-scoped; root .env unchanged.

limits: The review covered SystemEvents and DuplicateFixLog retained text; other retained user-authored free-text columns still require classification.
Verification uses the current ORM/Alembic schema, not a deployed operator schema.
